posts.text: This May Day, we honor the workers who keep our city moving. We must continue the fight for fair wages, safe conditions, and dignity on the job for every worker.

The Supreme Court’s insidious assault on Section 2 is likely to trigger the worst collapse of minority representation since the failure of Reconstruction—not by accident but by design.

Bronx programs serve nearly 43% of New York State's TRIO Talent Search and EOC students. The Trump Administration's FY26 grant applications would cut both programs by two-thirds and shift TRIO away from college access.

My Bronx colleagues and I are fighting Secretary McMahon for the Bronx students who depend on them.

The Supreme Court has effectively gutted the Voting Rights Act.

Section 2 was one of the last ways to challenge racial vote dilution. As Justice Kagan wrote in the dissent, states can now 'systematically dilute minority citizens' voting power' without legal consequence.

This is unacceptable. Congress must restore what this Court has destroyed.

The sheer speed, scale, and structure of the trades are deeply suspicious. Ask yourself, what kind of trader would make a massive trade 15 minutes before a market-moving presidential announcement with billions of dollars at stake and without a hedge? The only plausible answer to that question is an insider.
